body:
See

```
The value must be unique amongst all the IDs in the element's home subtree and must 
contain at least one character. The value must not contain any space characters.
```

The [HTML5 draft](http://www.w3.org/html/wg/drafts/html/master/dom.html#the-id-attribute) states that "There are no other restrictions on what form an ID can take"

In HTML4 it was relevant that it started with a "a-z" char. That is still the case, though.
@dereuromark true but a bc break is a bug

The bug - as we discussed quite thoroughly - was a different and more severe one (and was a faulty implementation to begin with) which has been resolved now.

EDIT: maybe we can exclude some more special characters. But that would highly increase the risk of collisions again.
Providing the FormHelper with a setting to behave either way (old collisisions vs collision free) sounds less optimal to me.
I know we discussed this before, but at the time I was more or less assuming it would go in a minor release - not a bug fix... preventing duplicate ids is not === change the way ids are generated.
I think the original change is still a good one. I've removed `@` from id attributes. Are there any other characters that should also be filtered out?
@markstory wouldn't it be better to find a regex that is all valid ID characters and remove all the ones that don't fall in that list?
@josegonzalez The list is pretty permissive for HTML5 and pretty restrictive for html4/xhtml.

We might have to go with the restrictiveness for BC's sake. This way the DOM ids would not change by default but only if there is a collision. I guess that would solve the BC breaking issue here.
For 3.0 it will be resolved then via different id generation anyway.

body:
For 3.0 stick with the xhtml/html4 strictness\* and find some way to auto-convert/escape symbols that don't fit thus not generating collisions? possible?

*if not, as soon as one declares html5 as XML you will have issues here and generating xml valid applications is no longer easy using cake.
@jhli I would prefer to use the XML compatible versions of HTML5 personally. Sticking with html4/xhtml means no HTML5 form elements for one.

@markstory as long as its XML compatible, fine, screw HTML4.
At least for HTML5 it does not matter if served as application/xhtml+xml or text/html - for both cases the trailing slash for void elements works, afaik (no juggling required by the framework)
Right now all the HTML the helpers generate is XML friendly as far as the attributes and tag names go. Even if we did change that the tag sets and attribute formatting can easily be replaced.
